title: Release Highlights Schema
description: The short, user-facing rows for one release, in releases/<version>.yaml, or for main since the last release, in releases/unreleased.yaml. `paramify update` shows the rows that are new between the commit you run and the one you move to, and, in `fetchers`, one line per fetcher that changed, instead of the CHANGELOG, which is written for maintainers and runs to thousands of lines. See releases/README.md.

version.description: The release, as its CHANGELOG heading writes it and without the tag's leading v (0.6.0-beta for tag v0.6.0-beta), or `unreleased` for the file that collects rows on main between releases. Must equal the file's basename.

date.description: Release date. Optional: the CHANGELOG heading's date is used when this is absent.

highlights.description: Rows of what is new, plus one `breaking` row per Breaking entry in the CHANGELOG.

fetchers.description: One line per fetcher that changed in the release, drafted at release time. `paramify update` shows the lines for the fetchers the user's manifests use.

version.description: The fetcher's version in this release.

note.description: One line on what changed, for the person running the fetcher.

draft.description: True while the line is a draft. A release cannot ship with a draft mark.

tag.description: The pill shown before the title. `breaking` rows are listed apart from the rest, before the confirm prompt, with their `fix`.

title.description: One line a user understands without the CHANGELOG. Say what they get or must do, not how it was built.

detail.description: Optional second line, shown dimmed under the title.

try.description: Optional command to try the change, shown in the closing panel. Must be a paramify command.

fix.description: What the user does about a breaking change. Required on `breaking` rows.

fetchers.description: Fetcher names the change affects. Shell-style globs work (okta_*). A breaking row with fetchers names each of the user's manifests that uses one. A breaking row with neither `fetchers` nor `custom_fetchers` is treated as touching everyone.

draft.description: True while the row is a draft. A release cannot ship with a draft mark.

custom_fetchers.description: True when the change affects only fetchers the user wrote themselves (a change to the fetcher contract that no shipped fetcher is affected by). The row then touches only clones that have their own fetcher directories.
